examples.japanese: {猫|ねこ}が{鼠|ねずみ}を{追|お}いかけている。
examples.english: The cat is chasing the mouse.

examples.japanese: {台所|だいどころ}で{鼠|ねずみ}が{走|はし}り{回|まわ}る{音|おと}がした。
examples.english: I heard the sound of a mouse running around in the kitchen.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{家|いえ}に{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}したら、{天井裏|てんじょううら}で{鼠|ねずみ}が{走|はし}る{音|おと}が{聞|き}こえて{困|こま}った。
examples.english: After moving into an old house, I was troubled by the sound of mice running in the ceiling.

examples.japanese: {昔|むかし}は{鼠|ねずみ}が{米|こめ}を{食|た}べてしまうので、{農家|のうか}の{人|ひと}たちは{猫|ねこ}を{飼|か}って{鼠|ねずみ}を{追|お}い{払|はら}っていた。
examples.english: In the past, mice would eat the rice, so farmers kept cats to chase them away.

notes:
{鼠|ねずみ} is the general term for mice and rats - small rodents found worldwide.

KANJI:
The kanji {鼠|ねずみ} is complex (13 strokes) and often written in hiragana as ねずみ in everyday use.

TYPES:
- {家鼠|いえねずみ}: house mouse
- {溝鼠|どぶねずみ}: brown rat, sewer rat
- {野鼠|のねずみ}: field mouse
- ハムスター: hamster (a popular pet)

CHINESE ZODIAC ({十二支|じゅうにし}):
- {子|ね} is the first of the twelve zodiac animals
- {子年|ねどし}: Year of the Rat
- People born in rat years are said to be clever and resourceful

EXPRESSIONS AND IDIOMS:
- {窮鼠|きゅうそ}{猫|ねこ}を{噛|か}む: a cornered rat will bite a cat (desperation leads to unexpected action)
- {鼠算|ねずみざん}: exponential growth (like mouse reproduction)
- {袋|ふくろ}の{鼠|ねずみ}: a rat in a bag (trapped with no escape)
- {鼠|ねずみ}一匹{通|とお}さない: not letting even a mouse through (airtight security)

COLOR:
{鼠色|ねずみいろ}: mouse-gray (a muted gray color popular in traditional Japanese aesthetics)

CULTURE:
- Mice/rats have mixed symbolism in Japan
- Associated with {大黒天|だいこくてん} (god of wealth) - mice are his messengers
- Also seen as pests that damage crops and spread disease

RELATED VOCABULARY:
- {猫|ねこ}: cat (natural predator)
- {罠|わな}: trap
- {齧歯類|げっしるい}: rodent
